ChangedDecoders: Aztec one- and two-pixel modules retain their centre value instead of a 3x3 majority crossing module boundaries; larger modules retain noise averaging.

Aztec image recognition locates nested square bullseyes away from the image centre, fits their raster edges and samples the data grid through the existing projective transform. Search is bounded to 1024 pixels per axis, four contrast-derived thresholds, two polarities and eight ring candidates per pass, with cancellation and existing framing, ECC and payload checks.

Four-connected binary component traversal is shared by Aztec and Data Matrix, preserving the existing Data Matrix component priority and selection. Pooled scratch buffers remain owned by the image search.
No public API, production dependency, comparison hint, oracle, scoring rule, total timeout or recognition allowance changes.
AttributionLimits: This follow-up records 205/267 correct positive images versus 198/267 in the previous pass. Previously correct images lost: none; gained: aztec-1/7.png, aztec-2/19.png, aztec-2/15.png, aztec-2/13.png, aztec-2/14.png, aztec-2/17.png, aztec-2/10.png. Paired negative completion is [27, 29, 30, 30]/31 with the current binary and [28, 29, 30, 29]/31 with the previous qualified binary. All outcomes remain sensitive to shared-host contention and wall-clock budgets; no universal timeout or recognition advantage is established. Aztec sampling and perspective recognition recover measured failures without changing total or family recognition allowances. Demonstrated regression gains do not establish accuracy on unseen photographs. Supplemental PDF417 images are regression evidence informed by prior remediation, not an unseen holdout. The invalid GS1 AI (3922) oracle and undeclared QR character encoding policies remain unchanged in scoring. Stacked DataBar and Expanded Stacked multiple-symbol localization and arbitrary perspective remain unproved; MaxiCode image scanning is unsupported.
